lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: lines of fit

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: Ice-cream sales and sunburn reports rise together. What can be concluded?

steps: Identify the quantities and the applicable model.
Check that the result answers the question.
workedSolution.answer: They are correlated; this alone does not prove causation.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Umbrella sales and rainy-day traffic delays are correlated. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: They are correlated; this alone does not prove causation.
There is no relationship at all.

items.prompt: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with radius 4 units and height 6 units. Express your answer as a rational multiple of π.
Find the exact volume of a cone with radius 6 units and height 9 units. Express your answer as a rational multiple of π.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Find the exact volume of a sphere with radius 3 units. Express your answer as a rational multiple of π.
A cylinder and cone each have radius 3 units and height 12 units. Which has the greater volume?
As x increases, y shows no consistent change. What association does this scatter plot describe?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Most plotted points follow y = 2x + 1. Of these points, (6, 13), (7, 15), (5, 11), (6, 25), which point is an outlier?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A line of fit is y = 2x + 5. Predict y when x = 5.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
